sections.title: Why Singapore Conditions Affect Floor Care

blocks.text: Singapore's climate plays a real role in how floors here need to be maintained.

Humidity and heat: Marble stays cool underfoot, which is part of why it's popular here, but the same porous stone is sensitive to moisture and acidic spills, so Singapore's humid climate makes regular sealing and careful cleaning more important.
Timber movement: Parquet expands and contracts as humidity shifts between air-conditioned rooms and open corridors, which can loosen boards and wear the varnish down over time.
Grit from daily traffic: Fine grit tracked in from HDB corridors, condo car parks, and lift lobbies acts like sandpaper on tiled and marble floors underfoot.

about.title: About Pro Surface Works | Singapore Floor Restoration
about.description: Founded in 2016 by Tanvir Rahman, Pro Surface Works is an in-house floor and marble restoration team of 25 to 30 technicians across Singapore.

blocks.text: Tanvir Rahman is an electrical engineer who moved into business ownership. He first established Luminous Engineering Pte Ltd in 2015, and about a year later founded Pro Surface Works in 2016 as a sole proprietorship, moving into floor, marble, and surface restoration work.

Pro Surface Works has been operating since 2016. The company grew from a small operation into an in-house team of 25 to 30 technicians, serving residential and commercial clients across Singapore without subcontracting the work out.

Tanvir Rahman is the founder and Managing Director of Pro Surface Works. He has 12 years of experience in the industry, and his background as an electrical engineer carries into how the company approaches its work.

Assessing a floor problem, in his view, starts with identifying the underlying cause, such as moisture ingress, grout failure, or a worn protective coating, rather than only treating the visible symptom. That approach shapes how the in-house team is trained to assess jobs before recommending polishing, restoration, repair, or replacement.

Pro Surface Works runs with an in-house team of 25 to 30 technicians. The work is not subcontracted out, so the technician who carries out the site assessment is typically involved in the job itself, from the initial visit through to completion.
Keeping the team in-house is also how the company keeps its process and equipment consistent from one job to the next, rather than depending on outside crews with their own methods and tools.
The same six steps apply whether the job is a single room or a full commercial floor.
1. Assess the actual condition  of the surface, not just how it looks on top.
2. Identify the underlying issue,  such as moisture, wear, or material failure.
3. Decide whether polishing, restoration, repair, or replacement  is the appropriate response.
4. Select equipment and materials  suited to that specific surface and problem.
5. Carry out the work with the in-house team,  start to finish.
6. Review the finished result  against what was agreed at the quote stage.

The equipment and materials used on a job are matched to what that specific surface needs, not applied as one fixed process for every floor. Klindex machines are used for deep stone restoration and high-gloss planetary polishing on marble and stone floors, and a Lägler Hummel 8-inch sander is used for parquet sanding work.

Grout and sealant work is carried out with Mapei and Sika products, and Pereseal or Soudal sealants, depending on the job. Parquet varnishing uses Ronseal or Nippon finishes, depending on the required finish.

marble-stone-care.title: Marble & Stone Care in Singapore | Pro Surface Works
marble-stone-care.description: Professional marble and stone care in Singapore, from polishing to full restoration, for homes, condos, and commercial properties islandwide.

blocks.text: Marble & Stone Care covers the polishing, restoration, and surface maintenance Pro Surface Works provides for marble and natural stone surfaces across Singapore homes and businesses. It includes floors, kitchen countertops, and bathroom vanity or basin tops, in HDB flats, condominiums, landed properties, and commercial spaces.

The right treatment depends on the surface's actual condition. A floor that has simply lost its shine usually needs polishing, while cracks, etching, or deeper stains call for restoration. Countertops and vanity tops follow the same logic, assessed on-site before any work begins.
Four services sit under this category, each suited to a different starting condition.
Marble Floor Polishing
For marble floors that have dulled from everyday wear but aren't otherwise damaged. Polishing works the surface back to its original shine without addressing structural issues.
Explore Marble Floor Polishing →
Marble Restoration
For marble with cracks, etching, or deeper staining that polishing alone won't fix. Restoration addresses the actual damage before the surface is refinished.
Explore Marble Restoration →
Kitchen Countertop Polishing
For marble, granite, or solid-surface kitchen countertops that have scratched, dulled, or stained from daily use.
Explore Kitchen Countertop Polishing →
Vanity & Basin Top Polishing
For bathroom vanity and basin tops exposed to water, soap residue, and toiletries, which dull and stain differently than open floor areas.
Explore Vanity & Basin Top Polishing →

Marble is the primary surface across this category, on floors, countertops, and vanity or basin tops. Granite and other solid-surface materials are also covered specifically for kitchen and bathroom countertops, where the same polishing techniques apply.

Granite and terrazzo floors, homogeneous tile, and concrete are handled separately under General Floor Care, since floor-level hard surface work follows a different process than marble and countertop polishing.

sections.title: Common Problems With Marble & Stone Surfaces

blocks.text: “My marble floor has lost its shine.” This is usually surface wear or accumulated residue rather than damage, and it's often solved with polishing.
“There are scratches on the countertop.” Light scratches are typically cosmetic and treatable; deeper ones may need restoration rather than polishing.
“There's a dull patch where something acidic spilled.” This is etching, a reaction with the stone itself, and it needs restoration rather than a surface clean.
“The stone looks stained or discoloured.” Staining depends on what caused it and how long it's been there, confirmed during an on-site assessment.
“Some areas look more worn than others.” High-traffic spots wear faster than the rest of the floor, which is common near entrances and hallways.

sections.title: Can Marble Be Restored Instead of Replaced?

blocks.text: In many cases, yes. Worn or dull marble can usually be restored, but the right option depends on the depth and type of damage.
Restoration may be considered when: the wear is mainly cosmetic, scratches or etching are within a treatable depth, and the stone is still structurally sound.
Replacement may be considered when: the damage is extensive, the stone is structurally compromised, or restoration is unlikely to give a practical result.

Singapore's indoor climate, humidity, air-conditioning, and the grit tracked in from corridors and car parks, can all influence how marble and stone surfaces hold up over time. This doesn't mean every floor needs constant attention, but it's part of why the right maintenance interval varies from one property to the next.

sections.title: How We Approach Marble & Stone Care

blocks.text: Assess: the surface, floor, countertop, or vanity top, is examined on-site to see its actual condition.
Identify: the cause is identified, whether that's wear, etching, staining, or structural damage.
Recommend: the appropriate service is recommended, polishing, restoration, or a more specific treatment for the surface type.
Restore: the work is carried out with equipment matched to the stone's condition and finish.

Different stone conditions and finish requirements call for different levels of grinding, honing, or polishing, so the equipment used depends on the job. Klindex machines are used for deep stone restoration and high-gloss planetary polishing on marble and stone surfaces.
Examples of completed marble and stone work across Singapore are on the Projects page.
View Marble & Stone Projects →
Can all marble floors be restored?

Most marble floors can be restored to some degree, but the outcome depends on how deep the damage is and the condition of the stone underneath. A site assessment confirms whether polishing, restoration, or a more targeted treatment is the right fit before any work begins.
How do I know whether my marble needs polishing or restoration?

If the floor has simply dulled with everyday wear, polishing is usually enough. If there are scratches, etching, cracks, or deeper stains, restoration is typically needed first. The team can confirm which applies during a free assessment.
Can scratches and etching be removed from marble?

Light scratches and etching can often be treated through restoration, which addresses the surface rather than just adding shine. Deeper damage may limit how much can be corrected, which is why the actual depth of the mark matters more than how it looks at first glance.
How often should marble floors be maintained?

This depends on foot traffic, location, and how the floor is cleaned day to day. Commercial spaces with heavy traffic typically need attention more often than a quiet residential room, so there's no fixed schedule that applies to every property.
Can kitchen countertops and vanity tops be polished?
Yes. Kitchen countertops and bathroom vanity or basin tops are polished using the same principles as floors, adjusted for the material and how the surface is used day to day.
Does Pro Surface Works work with other stone surfaces?

Marble is the main focus of this category, along with granite and solid-surface materials on countertops and vanity tops. Other hard floor types, such as granite or terrazzo flooring, homogeneous tile, and concrete, are covered separately under General Floor Care.

grouting.title: Grouting Services in Singapore | Pro Surface Works
grouting.description: Regrouting, marble gum grouting, and epoxy grouting in Singapore, for bathrooms, kitchens, and tiled surfaces, from an in-house team islandwide.

blocks.text: Grout does more than fill the gap between tiles. It affects how a surface looks, how well it resists water and staining, and how long the tiles around it stay in good condition. When grout cracks, discolours, or comes loose, the problem usually gets worse rather than better on its own.
Three services sit under this category, each suited to a different grout problem or goal.
Cement-Based Regrouting
For standard grout that has cracked, discoloured, or deteriorated over time. This removes the old grout where needed and replaces it with new cement-based grout, matched to the tile and joint size.
Explore Cement-Based Regrouting →
Marble Gum Grouting

For homogeneous, porcelain, or granite tiles where the old grout lines are replaced with marble gum for a seamless, glossy, marble-like finish. This is a different technique from standard regrouting, suited to tiles where a smoother, more uniform joint is wanted.
Explore Marble Gum Grouting →
Epoxy Grouting

A waterproof, stain-resistant grout upgrade, generally used in kitchens, bathrooms, and other wet areas, or for new tile installations. Epoxy grouting is a material upgrade rather than a like-for-like repair for existing cement grout.
Explore Epoxy Grouting →

“Why is the grout in my bathroom turning dark?” Mould, moisture, and soap residue build up in porous grout over time, which is often a sign it needs cleaning or replacing rather than just a fresh scrub.
“The grout is cracking or crumbling.” This usually means the grout has reached the end of its lifespan and needs to be removed and replaced.
“Some grout lines are missing completely.” Missing grout exposes the tile edges and the surface underneath to water, which should be addressed rather than left as is.
“The grout feels loose or hollow when I press on it.” This can mean the grout has failed to bond properly and needs to be replaced.
“There's a musty smell near the tiles.” This is often linked to moisture trapped in or behind damaged grout.

sections.title: Does Your Grout Need Cleaning or Regrouting?

blocks.text: Cleaning may be appropriate when: the grout is structurally sound and the main issue is surface dirt or staining.
Regrouting may be appropriate when: the grout is cracked, missing, loose, or significantly deteriorated.
The right approach depends on the condition of the existing grout, confirmed during an on-site assessment.

Grouting work is most often needed in bathrooms, kitchens, and shower areas, where tiles are exposed to constant moisture. It also comes up in living areas, common areas, and commercial spaces with tiled or stone flooring, wherever grout lines have worn down or been affected by water.
Inspect: the existing grout is examined for cracking, staining, looseness, or missing sections.
Identify: the underlying issue is identified, whether that's age, moisture, or a material mismatch.
Select: the appropriate grout system is selected, cement-based, marble gum, or epoxy, based on the tile and the problem.
Complete: the work is completed and the finish checked before the job is signed off.

Grout choice depends on the tile type, how much moisture the area sees, and the finish a client wants. Mapei and Sika grout products are used for cement-based and epoxy grouting work, selected to suit the specific job.
Examples of completed regrouting, marble gum grouting, and epoxy grouting work across Singapore are on the Projects page.
View Our Projects →
How do I know if my grout needs cleaning or replacement?

If the grout is structurally sound and just dirty or stained, cleaning is usually enough. If it's cracked, missing, loose, or crumbling, replacement is the more practical option. A site assessment confirms which applies.
How long does regrouting usually take?
This depends on the size of the area and how much of the existing grout needs to be removed first. Most bathroom or kitchen jobs are completed within a few days, confirmed during the quote.
Can you regrout bathroom and kitchen areas?
Yes. Bathrooms and kitchens are two of the most common areas for regrouting, since tiles there are exposed to constant moisture and daily use.
What is the difference between cement-based and epoxy grout?

Cement-based grout is the standard, more affordable option and is what most existing grout lines are made of. Epoxy grout is a waterproof, stain-resistant upgrade, generally used in wet areas or new installations rather than as a direct repair.
Can damaged marble grout joints be replaced?

Yes. Marble and stone joints can be regrouted or refinished with marble gum grouting, depending on the tile type and the look a client wants. This is assessed alongside any wider Marble & Stone Care needs.
How do I choose the right grouting solution?

The right choice depends on the tile type, the condition of the existing grout, and how the area is used. The team can recommend the appropriate option, cement-based, marble gum, or epoxy, during a free assessment.

general-floor-care.title: General Floor Care in Singapore | Pro Surface Works
general-floor-care.description: Floor polishing, buffing, and refinishing for homogeneous tile, granite, terrazzo, and concrete floors across Singapore, from an in-house team.

sections.title: When Your Floor Needs More Than Routine Cleaning

blocks.text: A floor that used to mop up fine sometimes stops responding to regular cleaning. The shine doesn't come back the way it used to. Traffic areas near doorways or aisles start to look noticeably different from the rest of the room. Scuff marks and light scratches stay visible no matter how the floor is cleaned.

These are usually signs that the floor's finish, not just its surface dirt, has worn down or aged past what routine mopping can fix. That's the point where polishing, buffing, or refinishing becomes the relevant option rather than another round of cleaning product.

sections.title: Hard Floor Surfaces We Care For

blocks.text: Homogeneous tiles: common in HDB and condo units, these show wear as a dulled or scratched glaze, usually addressed with polishing.
Granite: a dense, hard-wearing floor material that still loses its finish over time, particularly in high-traffic commercial areas.
Terrazzo: common in older properties and common areas, terrazzo often needs grinding and polishing to bring back its original aggregate finish.
Concrete: used in warehouses, car parks, and some commercial units, concrete floors are typically refinished rather than polished to a high shine.
This category covers two services, depending on how far the floor's finish has deteriorated.
Floor Polishing & Buffing
For floors that have dulled or scuffed but still have a workable finish underneath. This restores shine and evens out the surface without a full refinish.
Explore Floor Polishing & Buffing →
Floor Refinishing & Restoration
For floors where the existing finish has worn through, or the surface has deeper scratches, staining, or unevenness that polishing alone won't correct.
Explore Floor Refinishing & Restoration →

sections.title: Which Floor Treatment Does Your Surface Need?

blocks.text: Polishing restores shine and appearance where the existing finish is still largely intact.
Buffing maintains or lightly improves the finish, depending on the floor type and how worn it is.
Refinishing addresses floors where the existing finish has broken down and needs more substantial treatment.
The right treatment depends on the flooring material, the existing finish, and the condition of the surface, confirmed on-site rather than guessed from a description over the phone.
A dull finish that no longer reflects light the way it used to
Uneven appearance between high-traffic and low-traffic areas
Scuff marks that don't lift with regular cleaning
Surface scratches from furniture, footwear, or equipment
Worn patches near entrances, aisles, or walkways
A finish that has visibly deteriorated or started flaking
Difficulty getting the floor back to how it originally looked

sections.title: For Homes, Offices, and Shared Spaces

blocks.text: Homes and HDB or condo units usually see this kind of wear in kitchens, living areas, and corridors, where foot traffic is heaviest. Offices, retail units, and other commercial premises tend to see it faster, simply because more people cross the same floor every day. Common areas and shared lobbies fall somewhere in between, with wear patterns shaped by how the space is actually used rather than its size alone.

sections.title: Floor Care in Singapore's Everyday Environment

blocks.text: Foot traffic, dust, and grit carried in from outside all play a part in how quickly a hard floor's finish wears down, and Singapore's humidity can add to that over time. This doesn't mean every floor here needs constant attention. It does mean the right maintenance interval depends on how the space is used, not a fixed schedule that applies everywhere.

sections.title: How We Determine the Right Treatment

blocks.text: Before recommending a treatment, the team considers the flooring material, the existing finish, the visible wear, and the overall condition of the surface. That assessment usually covers:
Identifying the floor material
Checking the surface condition
Determining the existing finish
Recommending the suitable treatment

sections.title: Professional Equipment for Hard Floor Care

blocks.text: Klindex machines, the same planetary grinding and polishing equipment used across the company's stone and marble work, are also used for homogeneous tile, granite, terrazzo, and concrete floors, with the grinding and polishing level adjusted to the surface and its condition.
Examples of completed floor polishing, buffing, and refinishing work across Singapore are on the Projects page.
View Our Projects →
How do I know whether my floor needs polishing or refinishing?

If the finish is largely intact and the floor has just lost its shine, polishing is usually enough. If the finish has worn through or the surface has deeper damage, refinishing is the more likely option. A site visit confirms which applies.
Can dull homogeneous tiles be polished?
Yes. Homogeneous tiles are one of the most common floor types this category covers, and a dulled glaze is usually addressed with polishing rather than a full refinish.
Is floor buffing suitable for every type of hard floor?

Not always. Buffing works best when the existing finish is still in reasonable condition. Floors with deeper wear or damage typically need refinishing instead, which is confirmed during the assessment.
Can scratches and scuff marks be removed?
Light scratches and scuff marks can often be polished out. Deeper scratches may need refinishing to fully correct, depending on how far they go into the surface.
How often should hard floors be professionally maintained?
This depends on foot traffic and how the space is used, not a fixed schedule. A commercial floor with heavy daily traffic will typically need attention sooner than a quiet residential room.
Can you assess the condition of an existing floor before recommending a treatment?
Yes. Every job starts with an on-site assessment of the floor's material, finish, and condition, so the recommendation is based on the actual surface rather than a general assumption.

parquet-flooring.description: Parquet flooring installation, polishing, sanding, varnishing, and repair across Singapore homes and businesses, from an in-house team islandwide.

sections.title: New Parquet Floor or Existing Floor?

blocks.text: Most people land on this page for one of two reasons, and the right next step depends on which one applies.
Installing New Parquet
Choosing a parquet material, preparing the subfloor, and having it installed properly from the start. Explore Parquet Flooring Installation.
Restoring an Existing Parquet Floor
Dullness, scratches, a worn finish, or damaged planks on a floor that's already down. The relevant service depends on what's actually wrong with it, covered in the sections below.
Seven services sit under this category. Each addresses a different stage or problem, from a brand new floor to one that needs its varnish stripped back before anything else can happen.
Parquet Flooring Installation
For new parquet floors, from material selection and subfloor preparation through to the finished installation.
Explore Parquet Flooring Installation →
Parquet Floor Polishing
For existing parquet that has lost its shine but doesn't need sanding, a lighter maintenance option that refreshes the surface.
Explore Parquet Floor Polishing →
Parquet Repair & Restoration
For warped, loose, cracked, or missing planks, where the problem is physical damage rather than a dull finish.
Explore Parquet Repair & Restoration →
Parquet Floor Sanding & Varnishing
The full refinishing process for floors that need more than polishing, sanding back the surface before a new varnish coat and finish.
Explore Parquet Floor Sanding & Varnishing →
Staircase Sanding & Varnishing
The same refinishing process, applied to parquet or timber staircases, which wear differently than open floor areas.
Explore Staircase Sanding & Varnishing →
Old Varnish Removal
For floors where the existing varnish has peeled, yellowed, or failed, and needs to be stripped back before any refinishing can begin.
Explore Old Varnish Removal →
Skirting Installation & Repair
For skirting boards that need installing alongside new parquet, or repairing where they've come loose or been damaged.
Explore Skirting Installation & Repair →

sections.title: Signs Your Parquet Floor May Need Professional Care

blocks.text: A dull or faded finish that no longer catches the light
Scratches or surface marks that stand out under closer look
Worn patches in high-traffic areas like hallways or living rooms
Varnish that's peeling, yellowing, or flaking off
Individual planks that are warped, loose, or visibly damaged
An uneven appearance from one part of the floor to another
Old, discoloured varnish that needs stripping before anything else
Skirting boards that are damaged, loose, or missing

sections.title: What Does Your Parquet Floor Need?

blocks.text: Polishing improves the surface appearance and finish where the floor is otherwise in good shape.
Sanding is more substantial preparation, used when the existing finish or surface needs to come back to bare wood.
Varnishing follows sanding, adding the protective and visual finish once the surface has been prepared.
The appropriate treatment depends on the parquet's condition, its existing finish, and the result you want to achieve.

Installing new parquet starts with assessing whether the space suits it, choosing a suitable material, and preparing the subfloor properly before anything is laid. Getting the preparation right at this stage is what determines how the floor performs later, not just how it looks on day one.

Timber moves with changes in humidity and temperature, and Singapore's mix of air-conditioned rooms and open, humid corridors gives parquet more of that movement to deal with than it would see in a drier, more stable climate. Over time, that can affect how boards sit and how long a finish lasts, which is part of why parquet care here is assessed on the actual floor rather than a fixed timeline.

sections.title: How We Assess an Existing Parquet Floor

blocks.text: The condition of an existing parquet floor determines whether it needs polishing, sanding, refinishing, repair, or a combination of treatments. The assessment looks at:
The condition of individual parquet blocks or planks
The existing finish and how far it's worn
Surface wear across different areas of the floor
Any previous repairs already carried out
Moisture-related concerns, where relevant

Ronseal and Nippon finishes are used for parquet varnishing, matched to the matte or glossy result a client wants. The right finish depends on the wood, how the floor is used, and the look the space calls for.
Examples of completed parquet installation, sanding, and restoration work across Singapore are on the Projects page.
View Our Projects →
Can an old parquet floor be restored?
In most cases, yes. Whether it needs polishing, sanding and refinishing, or repair for damaged planks depends on the condition of the floor, confirmed during an on-site assessment.
Should parquet flooring be polished or sanded?

Polishing suits a floor that's simply lost its shine. Sanding is for floors where the existing finish or surface needs to be taken back before refinishing. The team can confirm which applies to yours.
How often does parquet flooring need refinishing?
This depends on foot traffic, sunlight exposure, and how the floor has been maintained, not a fixed interval. Heavily used areas typically need attention sooner than quieter rooms.
Can damaged parquet blocks be repaired?
Yes. Warped, loose, cracked, or missing planks can usually be repaired individually, without refinishing the entire floor, depending on how widespread the damage is.
Can old varnish be removed before refinishing?
Yes. Where the existing varnish has peeled, yellowed, or failed, it's stripped back first, since sanding and varnishing over a failed finish won't give a lasting result.
Can parquet flooring be installed in Singapore homes?
Yes. Parquet is installed in HDB flats, condominiums, and landed homes across Singapore, with the subfloor preparation and material choice suited to the space and how it's used.

timber-wood-repair.title: Timber & Wood Repair in Singapore | Pro Surface Works
timber-wood-repair.description: Timber and wood repair, restoration, and refinishing for doors, furniture, cabinets, and window frames across Singapore, from an in-house team.

sections.title: When Timber Needs Repair Rather Than Replacement

blocks.text: Not every damaged timber surface needs to be replaced. Scratches, dents, a worn finish, peeling varnish, discolouration, and general ageing are all things a piece of wood can usually be brought back from, rather than pulled out and swapped for something new.

The practical option depends on the type, depth, and extent of the damage. A scratched door and a water-damaged window frame don't call for the same answer, which is why this page starts with the timber itself rather than a list of services.

sections.title: Timber & Wood Surfaces We Work With

blocks.text: Wooden doors: scratches, worn finish, and warping from daily use and humidity are the most common issues.
Furniture: tables, cabinetry, and other wood furniture that has faded, scratched, or lost its original finish over time.
Cabinets: kitchen and built-in cabinetry where the surface has worn, chipped, or discoloured with regular use.
Window frames: timber frames exposed to weather and moisture, which can peel, discolour, or deteriorate faster than indoor surfaces.
Other suitable timber surfaces are considered on a case-by-case basis, depending on the material and the extent of the damage.
This covers three types of work, matched to what's actually wrong with the timber, rather than three separate services to choose between upfront.
Repair addresses physical damage or a specific defective area, without touching the rest of the surface.
Restoration is broader work that improves the appearance and condition of older or worn timber overall.
Refinishing applies a new finish once the existing one has deteriorated and the surface has been properly prepared.
Which of these applies, and how much of the surface it covers, is confirmed once the timber has actually been assessed.

sections.title: Common Problems With Timber & Wood Surfaces

blocks.text: “The varnish on my wooden door is peeling.” This usually means the finish has failed and needs to be removed before a new one is applied.
“There are scratches on the cabinet doors.” Light surface scratches are often repairable without refinishing the whole piece.
“The window frame looks faded and worn.” Sun and weather exposure wear timber down faster than indoor surfaces, and this is usually addressed with restoration.
“The furniture has water marks or stains.” Depending on how deep the mark goes, this can often be treated rather than requiring the piece to be replaced.
In many cases, yes, but the result depends on the type and extent of the damage, the condition of the underlying timber, and the existing finish.
Repair may be practical when: the damage is mainly surface-level, the timber remains structurally sound, and the existing finish can be removed or reworked.
Replacement may need consideration when: the timber is severely compromised, structural damage is extensive, or restoration wouldn't give a practical result.

sections.title: Timber Repair vs Parquet Flooring Services

blocks.text: Timber & Wood Repair focuses on non-floor timber surfaces, doors, furniture, cabinets, and window frames. If it's a parquet floor that needs attention, that's covered separately under Parquet Flooring, which handles installation, polishing, sanding, and repair specifically for parquet.

Singapore's humidity and the shift between air-conditioned indoor spaces and warmer, more humid conditions outside both affect how timber surfaces hold up over time, particularly for doors and window frames exposed to the outdoors. This doesn't mean every timber surface will need attention, but it's part of why the right approach depends on the specific piece rather than a general rule.
The team first considers the timber type, the extent of the damage, the existing finish, and whether the affected area can be practically restored. That covers:
The timber or surface type
How extensive the damage is
The existing finish
Whether repair or replacement is the more practical option

The right finish depends on what's already on the surface, the appearance a client wants, how much protection the piece needs, and how it's actually used day to day. Ronseal and Nippon finishes are used where revarnishing is required, matched to the result the client is after.
Examples of completed timber and wood repair work across Singapore are on the Projects page.
View Our Projects →
Can damaged timber be repaired instead of replaced?

In many cases, yes. Surface-level damage on structurally sound timber is usually repairable. More extensive or structural damage may make replacement the more practical option, confirmed during an assessment.
Can peeling varnish be removed and reapplied?
Yes. Peeling or failed varnish is stripped back before a new finish is applied, since revarnishing over a failed coat won't hold or look right.
Can wooden doors and window frames be restored?
Yes. Doors and window frames are two of the most common items this service covers, particularly where they've been exposed to weather or daily wear.
Can damaged furniture or cabinets be repaired?
Yes, in most cases. The approach depends on the type of damage, whether it's scratches, water marks, or a worn finish, and the condition of the piece underneath.
How do I know whether timber needs repair or refinishing?

If the damage is localised, like a scratch or a chip, repair is usually enough. If the whole surface's finish has deteriorated, refinishing is more likely the right approach. The team can confirm which applies.
Can you assess a timber surface before recommending a repair?
Yes. Every job starts with an assessment of the timber type, the damage, and the existing finish, so the recommendation is based on the actual piece rather than a guess.

wood-decking.title: Wood Decking Services in Singapore | Pro Surface Works
wood-decking.description: Wood decking installation, repair, and restoration for outdoor timber decks across Singapore homes and landed properties, from an in-house team.

sections.title: Outdoor Timber Decking Faces Different Demands

blocks.text: A deck sits outside, exposed to direct sunlight, rain, humidity, and whatever gets tracked onto it underfoot. That's a very different environment from an indoor timber floor or piece of furniture, and it wears differently as a result.

Outdoor decking care isn't the same as indoor timber care. The boards, the finish, and the frame underneath all need to hold up against conditions an indoor surface never sees, which is why this page focuses specifically on decking rather than timber in general.

sections.title: Are You Installing a New Deck or Restoring an Existing One?

blocks.text: Both situations are covered under the same service, since a new installation and an existing deck's repair or restoration both come down to the same on-site assessment before work begins.
New decking: timber selection, subframe and surface preparation, and installation for a deck that isn't there yet.
Existing decking: repair for damaged boards, or restoration for a deck that's faded, worn, or weathered but still structurally usable.
Explore Wood Deck Installation & Repair →

sections.title: How to Tell When a Timber Deck Needs Attention

blocks.text: Colour that's faded noticeably from the original timber tone
A greyed, weathered appearance across the surface
Splinters or a rough surface underfoot
Cracked, split, or otherwise damaged boards
A finish that's worn away or no longer protecting the wood
Staining from standing water, leaves, or debris
Loose or damaged sections, particularly near edges or joints
Areas that show heavier wear than the rest of the deck

sections.title: Does Your Deck Need Repair or Replacement?

blocks.text: Not every weathered deck needs to be replaced. The practical option depends on the condition of the boards, the extent of the damage, and the overall structure underneath.
Repair or restoration may be considered when: the damage is limited, the boards remain usable, the wear is mainly finish-related, or the affected sections can be treated or replaced individually.
Replacement may need consideration when: the damage is extensive, the structural integrity is compromised, or significant sections have deteriorated beyond a practical repair.

sections.title: Keeping a Timber Deck in Good Condition

blocks.text: A deck that's cleaned regularly, has debris cleared from between the boards, and gets its wear addressed early tends to need far less extensive work down the line than one that's left alone until it's visibly deteriorated. Keeping the surface finish in reasonable condition is part of what protects the timber underneath it, not just how the deck looks.

Outdoor timber in Singapore is exposed to moisture and strong sunlight throughout the year, so the condition of the finish and the boards needs to be assessed as part of ongoing care, rather than left until a problem becomes obvious. This doesn't mean every deck needs constant attention, but it's part of why outdoor timber is looked at differently from timber that stays indoors.

sections.title: Choosing a Suitable Decking Material and Finish

blocks.text: The right timber and finish for a deck depends on where it sits, how much sun and rain it's exposed to, the look a client wants, and how much upkeep they're willing to put in. A protective finish suited to outdoor exposure is part of what keeps a deck performing well, confirmed as part of the assessment rather than assumed upfront.

sections.title: Before We Recommend a Decking Treatment

blocks.text: The condition of the boards, the surface finish, and the areas of wear all influence whether a deck needs cleaning, refinishing, repair, or more extensive restoration. That assessment looks at:
Board condition
Surface finish
Visible damage
Moisture-related concerns
Overall usability
If it's an indoor timber surface, a door, cabinet, or window frame, rather than outdoor decking, that's covered separately under Timber & Wood Repair.
Examples of completed decking installation and restoration work across Singapore are on the Projects page.
View Our Projects →
How long can a timber deck last in Singapore?

This depends far more on maintenance and exposure than a fixed number of years. A deck that's cleaned regularly and has its finish maintained will generally outlast one that's left untreated in full sun and rain.
How do I know whether my deck needs sanding or replacement?

If the boards are structurally sound and the issue is mainly the surface or finish, sanding and refinishing is usually enough. If the damage goes deeper, replacement of the affected sections may be the more practical option, confirmed on-site.
Can faded timber decking be restored?
Yes, in most cases. Fading is typically a surface and finish issue rather than structural damage, and it's usually addressed through cleaning, sanding, and refinishing.
Can damaged decking boards be repaired individually?
Often, yes. Where the damage is limited to specific boards or sections, those can usually be treated or replaced without redoing the entire deck.
How often should an outdoor timber deck be maintained?
This depends on exposure and use rather than a fixed schedule. A deck in full sun and rain will typically need attention sooner than one that's sheltered.
Can you assess an existing deck before recommending a treatment?
Yes. Every job starts with an on-site assessment of the boards, the finish, and the overall condition of the deck, so the recommendation is based on the actual structure rather than a guess.

vinyl-flooring.title: Vinyl Flooring Services in Singapore | Pro Surface Works
vinyl-flooring.description: Vinyl flooring installation, repair guidance, and SPC vs LVT comparisons for Singapore homes and offices, from an in-house team islandwide.

sections.title: New Vinyl Flooring or an Existing Floor That Needs Attention?

blocks.text: This page splits into two directions, depending on where you're starting from.
New vinyl flooring: choosing between SPC and LVT, and getting it installed properly, covered below and on the Vinyl Flooring Installation page.

Existing vinyl flooring: damage, lifting, wear, or a floor that's reached the point where repair versus replacement needs deciding, which this page covers directly below since vinyl repair doesn't have a separate page of its own.

sections.title: SPC or LVT: Choosing Vinyl Flooring for Your Space

blocks.text: SPC (stone plastic composite) is the more rigid, water-resistant option, generally suited to areas with higher moisture exposure or heavier daily use. LVT (luxury vinyl tile) is more flexible and often chosen for its appearance and feel underfoot, and tends to suit lower-traffic residential rooms.

Which one fits depends on the area of use, expected foot traffic, the condition of the existing subfloor, and how the space needs to look and feel. If you're weighing vinyl against a natural hard floor instead, General Floor Care covers the homogeneous tile, granite, terrazzo, and concrete side of that comparison.
Explore General Floor Care →
Once the material is chosen, installation covers assessing the existing floor, preparing the subfloor, taking accurate measurements, and fitting it using the method suited to that material and space.
Explore Vinyl Flooring Installation →

sections.title: What Can Go Wrong With Vinyl Flooring?

blocks.text: “One section of my vinyl floor is lifting.” This is often related to moisture underneath or a weakened adhesive bond, and it usually gets worse if left alone.
“There are scratches and scuff marks near the entrance.” High-traffic areas near doors wear faster than the rest of the room, which is normal but still fixable.
“A section has torn or split.” Sharp impacts or heavy furniture can tear vinyl, and whether that section can be patched depends on where it is and how large the tear is.
“The colour looks patchy or faded in places.” Sunlight exposure and uneven wear can cause this, and it's more noticeable on some vinyl types than others.

sections.title: Should Vinyl Flooring Be Repaired or Replaced?

blocks.text: It depends on the extent and location of the damage, the condition of the surrounding flooring, and whether a practical repair is possible.
Repair may be considered when: the damage is limited, the affected section can be addressed on its own, and the surrounding flooring is still in usable condition.
Replacement may be considered when: the damage is extensive, multiple areas are affected, or the flooring has reached the end of its practical lifespan.

sections.title: Where Vinyl Flooring Can Be Used

blocks.text: Vinyl suits homes, offices, retail spaces, and other indoor commercial interiors where a durable, relatively low-maintenance floor is wanted without the cost or weight of natural stone or solid timber. It's a common choice for bedrooms and living areas, as well as office floors that need to handle daily foot traffic without heavy upkeep.

Singapore's humidity and the moisture that comes with it are part of why subfloor condition matters so much before installation, and why floors near bathrooms, kitchens, or windows are worth keeping an eye on over time. Vinyl generally handles moisture better than timber, but that doesn't mean every product or installation is unaffected, which is why the specifics are confirmed against the actual material chosen.
The condition of the existing flooring, the extent of the damage, and the condition of the underlying surface all influence whether repair or replacement is the more practical option. That covers:
Surface condition
Damage location
Extent of wear
Underlying floor condition
Condition of the surrounding flooring
Examples of completed vinyl flooring installation and repair work across Singapore are on the Projects page.
View Our Projects →
Can damaged vinyl flooring be repaired?
Often, yes, particularly for localised damage like a tear, a lifted section, or scratches. Whether a repair blends in well depends on the product and how noticeable the affected area is.
When should vinyl flooring be replaced instead of repaired?

When the damage is widespread, when multiple areas are affected, or when the flooring has generally reached the end of its useful life. A repair on a floor that's failing throughout usually isn't a practical fix.
Can vinyl flooring be installed over an existing floor?
In some cases, depending on the condition and type of the existing floor. This is confirmed during an assessment, since installing over an unsuitable surface can affect how the new flooring performs.
How long does vinyl flooring normally last?

This varies with the product quality, how the space is used, and how well it's installed and maintained, rather than a single fixed number. Higher-traffic areas will generally show wear sooner than quieter rooms.
Is vinyl flooring suitable for Singapore homes?

Yes. Vinyl is a common choice in Singapore homes for its durability and relatively low maintenance, and it handles humidity better than timber, though subfloor condition still matters for a good result.
How should vinyl flooring be maintained?
Regular cleaning and prompt attention to any lifting, scratches, or damage go a long way. Leaving a small problem unaddressed is usually what turns it into a larger repair later.
